question: What is the primary function of hospital policies in nursing practice?

options.A: To replace formal nursing education and clinical training
options.B: To increase the administrative workload of ward managers
options.C: To bridge healthcare laws and daily clinical actions
options.D: To eliminate the need for individualized patient care plans

explanation: Policies translate broader legal requirements into practical, everyday steps that guide safe bedside nursing care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why must nurses adhere strictly to institutional policies during patient care?

options.A: To ensure that doctors do not perform nursing duties
options.B: To protect patients, themselves, and the institution from harm
options.C: To speed up patient discharge processes in busy wards
options.D: To reduce the financial budget of the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Adhering to established policies ensures safe standards of practice, minimizing legal liability and preventable clinical errors. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h1)

question: What legal standard do hospital policies establish in a court of law?

options.A: The maximum penalty for professional misconduct and theft
options.B: The national budget allocation for tertiary health institutions
options.C: The salary scale for registered nurses and midwives
options.D: The expected standard of care for a competent practitioner

explanation: Courts and regulatory bodies use institutional policies to define what a competent nurse should do in a specific clinical situation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h2)

question: A nurse deviates from the ward medication protocol without clinical reason and harms a patient. What is this primarily classified as?

options.A: An interprofessional conflict with the pharmacist
options.B: An acceptable adaptation of routine ward duties
options.C: Professional negligence due to policy breach
options.D: A minor administrative error with no legal impact

explanation: Ignoring established safety protocols without a valid clinical justification exposes the nurse to claims of professional negligence. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which authority sits at the highest level of the healthcare policy hierarchy in Nigeria?

options.B: National laws and federal health acts

explanation: National legislation forms the supreme legal framework that governs all subordinate healthcare policies and regulations. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why must a departmental protocol align with hospital-wide policies?

options.A: Unit managers have no authority to write independent rules
options.B: Departmental protocols are only suggestions for junior staff
options.C: Subordinate rules cannot contradict higher authority directives
options.D: National laws forbid hospitals from having specialized units

explanation: The policy hierarchy dictates that lower-level unit protocols must always conform to broader hospital and national standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the key difference between hospital-wide policies and departmental protocols?

options.A: Their relevance to direct patient bedside care
options.B: The scope of personnel and areas they cover
options.C: The requirement for annual review by the government
options.D: Whether they are legally binding for nurses

explanation: Hospital-wide policies affect everyone in the facility, whereas departmental protocols target the specialized procedures of a specific unit. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h4)

question: A specialized intensive care protocol conflicts with a general hospital infection control policy. Which rule takes precedence?

options.C: Whichever rule the ward nurse prefers
options.D: The verbal order of the unit porter

explanation: General hospital-wide policies override specialized departmental protocols when a conflict arises between institutional standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is the typical timeframe for reviewing established hospital policies?

options.A: Every ten years by the federal ministry
options.C: Only when a major lawsuit occurs

explanation: Policies require periodic review every few years to incorporate new evidence, technology, and changes in regulatory standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why is frontline nurse participation crucial during the policy drafting stage?

options.A: Hospital management lacks the time to read medical textbooks
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of printing policy manuals
options.C: They are legally required to author all hospital administrative documents
options.D: They understand practical bedside realities and workflow challenges

explanation: Involving bedside nurses ensures that drafted policies are realistic, practical, and implementable in actual clinical environments. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why are nurses considered the primary drivers of healthcare policy implementation?

options.A: They have the sole authority to rewrite hospital bylaws
options.B: They alone decide which drugs are purchased by pharmacy
options.C: They form the largest workforce in the hospital
options.D: They manage the financial accounts of the clinical units

explanation: Due to their sheer numbers and continuous presence at the bedside, nurses are central to translating policies into daily practice. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h6)

question: A senior nurse notices junior colleagues ignoring a vital hand hygiene protocol during busy shifts. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Rewrite the hand hygiene protocol to lower the standards
options.B: Ignore the lapse since the ward is extremely busy today
options.C: Model correct compliance and mentor the staff on safety
options.D: Report the entire nursing shift directly to the police

explanation: Ward leaders must actively mentor colleagues and reinforce policy compliance rather than ignoring safety lapses during busy periods. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h6)

question: What does the term 'policy gap' refer to in a healthcare setting?

options.A: A situation where existing rules fail to address clinical challenges
options.B: The physical distance between the pharmacy and the medical ward
options.C: The time gap between two consecutive nursing shift handovers
options.D: The financial deficit in the hospital annual budgetary allocation

explanation: A policy gap occurs when current institutional rules do not adequately cover emerging clinical scenarios or practical realities. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h7)

question: Why is a non-punitive reporting culture essential when nurses notice policy deviations?

options.A: It guarantees that all policies will be abolished permanently
options.B: It ensures that nurses never face disciplinary action for crimes
options.C: It encourages honest reporting of near-misses and system flaws
options.D: It removes the need for any hospital administrative oversight

explanation: A blame-free reporting environment allows staff to highlight safety flaws and gaps openly, enabling continuous quality improvement. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h7)

question: How do standardized hospital policies directly improve patient safety?

options.A: By lowering the cost of medical equipment purchased abroad
options.B: By minimizing unwarranted clinical variation and medical errors
options.C: By reducing the number of patients admitted to emergency units
options.D: By increasing the speed of administrative paperwork processing

explanation: Uniform clinical procedures reduce practice variations, ensuring consistent, safe care delivery that prevents avoidable medical errors. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h8)

question: Which indicator best shows that a hospital policy is successfully driving quality improvement?

options.A: Fewer staff meetings held during the morning shift hours
options.B: Higher administrative fines paid for delayed documentation
options.C: An increase in the length of time nurses spend in offices
options.D: A measurable decrease in preventable adverse patient events

explanation: Successful quality improvement policies directly result in safer care and a reduction in preventable patient harm. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h8)
